# perglm <a href="https://github.com/ZiangNiu6/perglm"><img src="man/figures/logo.png" align="right" height="139" alt="perglm hex logo" /></a>

<!-- badges: start -->
<!-- badges: end -->

**perglm** provides permutation-calibrated, empirically studentized score tests
for an exposure in generalized linear models.

## Quick start

Supply the nuisance-only null model as the formula, and pass the exposure
separately as a numeric vector. The result is a standard R `htest` object.

```{r quick-start, eval=FALSE}
library(perglm)

set.seed(42)
dat <- data.frame(z1 = rnorm(120), z2 = rnorm(120),
                  x = rbinom(120, 1, 0.3))
dat$y <- rpois(120, exp(0.3 + 0.2 * dat$z1 - 0.1 * dat$z2 + 0.2 * dat$x))

set.seed(2026)
result <- perglm_test(
  y ~ z1 + z2,
  data = dat,
  exposure = dat$x,
  family = poisson(),
  B = 999L
)
result
result$p.value
```

The default alternative is `"two.sided"`; `"greater"` and `"less"` refer to
the exposure coefficient on the link scale. Set `keep_statistics = TRUE` to
retain the sampled scores in `result$permuted_statistics`. See `?perglm_test`
for supported families, assumptions, and fitting controls.

The getting-started vignette walks through this example and its output:

```{r open-vignette, eval=FALSE}
vignette("getting-started", package = "perglm")
```

Its source is in [`vignettes/getting-started.Rmd`](vignettes/getting-started.Rmd).

## Validation

The [validation report](validation/results/report.html) records a reproducible
study of 22,000 datasets, with 499 permutations per successful test. Across 12
regular Gaussian and Poisson null scenarios, rejection rates at the 5% level
ranged from 3.9% to 5.6%; all pointwise 95% binomial intervals included 5%.
The study also records power, variance misspecification, and failures with rare
exposures. Scripts, seeds, raw results, and exact small-sample checks are in
`validation/`.

The saved validation report records implementation checkpoint
[`27801a8`](https://github.com/ZiangNiu6/perglm/commit/27801a8).
Reanalyze the saved results from that checkout, or rerun the validation scripts
to record a fresh source snapshot after further changes.

Null preparation checks Bernoulli nuisance designs for separation and Gaussian
residuals for numerical resolution. These checks run once per null fit and
reject unsupported cases before permutations. The validation report includes
regressions for the separation and exact-fit cases found in the initial audit,
alongside valid offset models and small but numerically resolved noise.

## Development status

Internal helpers fit null GLMs and prepare their working score residuals,
weights, and cached projections. Supported families are Gaussian, Bernoulli,
Poisson, Gamma, inverse Gaussian, and negative binomial, including fixed offsets.
Model observations must be complete, with unit prior weights and a full-rank
nuisance design containing an intercept.

Rcpp kernels support scalar and batch studentization, as well as combined
exposure residualization and score calculation, alongside an R reference
implementation. Three additional internal helpers now provide:

- `glm_score_statistic()`: the observed score, with exposure alignment and
  residual-identifiability checks.
- `permutation_p_value()`: inclusive one- or two-sided tail comparisons with
  the plus-one correction.
- `calibrate_glm_permutation()`: fixed-budget label permutation using the
  cached null fit and bounded Rcpp batches. `set.seed()` controls the draws;
  retaining the permuted statistics is optional.

Each shuffle recomputes exposure residuals and empirical score variance.
Nonidentifiable exposures and undefined scores stop calibration without a
p-value; no draws are discarded or redrawn. The exported `perglm_test()` function
connects null fitting and calibration and returns the test result with null-fit
diagnostics.

The package layout includes R code in `R/`, native code in `src/`,
documentation in `man/`, tests in `tests/`, and pkgdown configuration for a future
website in `docs/`.

## Reference

Ai, J. and Niu, Z. (2026). *Conditional independence testing through marginal
permutation*. [arXiv:2611.03255](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.03255).
